git_commit_note: The commit immediately preceding the one that adds this file — the tree that was actually built and measured. See benchmarks/tpch/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md.
notes: Every engine and the benchmark runner ran inside the container stack. The runner is containerized because the DataFusion adapter executes in-process inside it; a host-side runner would measure DataFusion natively against containerized rivals.
arneb ran in its default configuration: zero ARNEB_* tuning variables, verified with docker inspect against the running container rather than the compose file.
arneb and Trino each received 3 nodes x 2 CPUs; the runner received 6 CPUs so DataFusion, a single process, had the same total budget.
No memory limits were set on any engine, matching the existing benchmark setup.
Numbers are arm64 macOS figures from one laptop. They are reproducible on comparable hardware; they do not generalize to Linux x86 servers.

q09 agrees across all three engines but sits on a rounding boundary in the twelfth significant digit, so its strict hashes differ while the coarser comparison matches. See the boundary note in comparison.md.
